children: has a plan set for a broad, global Oreo relaunch in 2027, according to Food Navigator. Notably, the relaunch is much more than just a new logo or cosmetic redesign.

The food company called the 360-degree Oreo refresh an initiative that could strengthen Oreo’s reach, relevance, and availability as the brand approaches $5B in annual revenue. In particular, the program is meant to attract consumers in markets where Oreo has comparatively low penetration while sustaining momentum in established markets such as the United States and China.

The Oreo relaunch will focus on improved packaging, expanded price-and-pack architecture, product-quality upgrades, and stronger brand activation. Broader price-pack architecture is expected to lead to more package sizes and price points, enabling Oreo to fit more shopping occasions and channels, ranging from small, affordable impulse purchases in convenience outlets to larger family and sharing packs. Mondelez

also plans new Oreo formulas in some cases, intended to improve product labels and quality. In a nod to the brand's past, Mondelez wants the relaunch to reinforce the recognizable "twist, lick, dunk" ritual.
Innovation will also be an important part of the new strategy. While Mondelez
already used extensions such as Oreo Minis, Thins, Gluten Free, and Zero Sugar to appeal to people who may not buy the traditional cookie, new flavoring options are expected in 2027.

Oreo’s history reaches back to 1912, when the first cookies were made at a bakery in Manhattan’s Chelsea Market and sold in bulk tins. The product was renamed the Oreo Sandwich in 1921, became the Oreo Crème Sandwich in 1937, and steadily developed its distinct identity around two chocolate wafers and a sweet crème filling.

Oreo broadened beyond the original cookie after Double Stuf debuted in the U.S. in 1974. White Fudge Covered Oreos arrived as a holiday product in 1990. Global expansion was also important as the brand was sold in 30 countries by 1993, and Oreo became China’s top-selling biscuit in 2006. Today Oreo products are sold in more than 100 nations.

title: Mondelez plans a major update to the iconic Oreo brand
